data.title: Profile
data.tagline: A named and saved collection of configuration settings for switching between work, personal, or different provider environments.
data.learningOutcome: You can isolate connection settings with named profiles and distinguish them from workspaces and branches.
data.description: For example, work and personal projects may use separate Providers, Base URLs, key variable names, or permission settings saved as work and personal profiles. Selecting a profile loads its configuration; it does not switch git branches, project files, or conversation history, and it does not replace checking the actual endpoint and credential source.

learning.assumes: You need to switch an AI tool between more than one project or account.
learning.outcome: You can isolate connection settings with named profiles and distinguish them from workspaces and branches.

distinctions.label: Configuration File
distinctions.explanation: A Configuration File is the physical file on disk; a Profile is a named preset group defined within configurations for quick context switching.

explanation.title: It names a settings group
explanation.text: Related Provider, Base URL, model, and permission settings can be saved as one named combination.

explanation.title: Select one at startup
explanation.text: When the tool starts with an explicit profile, the client initializes the session from that group.

explanation.title: It reduces manual switching errors
explanation.text: Separate work and personal connections reduce the chance of sending code through the wrong endpoint.

data.boundary: A Profile is not a workspace, Git branch, or Session. It changes the AI client's connection settings, not local files, commit history, or conversation context.

lessonPractice.title: Which Profile workflow is safer for keeping sensitive project requests off public endpoints?

options.label: Explicitly select an isolated intranet Profile when starting the tool in the sensitive project
options.feedback: Correct. An explicit Profile loads the expected Provider and endpoint and reduces accidental use of a default configuration.

options.label: Put both company and personal keys in one default Profile for convenience
options.feedback: A shared default can route sensitive work through the wrong personal or public connection and does not isolate it.

options.label: Treat switching a Profile as switching a Git branch, so endpoint checks are unnecessary
options.feedback: A Profile changes AI connection settings, not code branches, and does not replace checking the Provider and Base URL.

data.agentPrompt: Check that the work and personal profiles use separate Providers, Base URLs, and key variable names. Do not read key values or change Git branches; show how to select a profile explicitly at startup.
